title: True shape of the Boomerang
caption: The Boomerang Nebula, imaged by ALMA and the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Boomerang Nebula · constellation Centaurus · about 5000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A purple double-lobed shape with a very narrow waist sits behind a more elongated orange shape in this view of the Boomerang Nebula. The purple is Hubble's visible-light view, and the orange is cold molecular gas seen by ALMA, the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, revealing the nebula's longer true shape.

The Boomerang is a protoplanetary nebula, about 5,000 light-years away, and since 2003 it has held the record as the coldest known object in the Universe. Astronomers think it grew out of the outer envelope of an ageing star after that star engulfed a smaller companion. That may explain its ultra-cold outflows, which are lit by the dying central star.

ALMA examined the dusty central disc and the outflows further out. Those outflows are colder even than the cosmic microwave background, the faint afterglow of the Big Bang, and they are expanding at 590 000 kilometers per hour.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (0.37 x 0.37 arcminutes) and distance (5000 light years), the frame spans roughly 0.5 × 0.5 light-years. Its light set out about 5,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This combines ALMA observations of carbon monoxide gas at submillimeter wavelengths (orange) with a visible-light Hubble image (purple).
filters: 880 μm · Radio 12CO (Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array Band 7)
understand.eye: The orange ALMA data trace submillimeter light from cold gas, which is invisible to the eye.

explore: The outflows stretch almost four light-years across the sky, and reach temperatures below -270 °C. The combined picture shows how different the same object can look depending on the kind of light used to observe it.
alt: A purple double-lobed nebula with a narrow center, overlaid with a longer orange shape of cold gas.
